Key.English: Someone else changed the setup while you were working on it.
set by the preset or the Load per cell option
How many cells a container gets when no rule draws it: its load from the config divided by this number. A smaller number means more cells. The Weight preset also sizes items by it.
No longer forced over the mission's own setup
Forced over the mission's own setup
Click one to open it. The cross takes that change back.
Nothing changed yet: the Default preset decides everything.
Imported config lines for %1 classes (%2 warnings). Save at Review puts them to use.
Imported config lines for %1 classes (%3 warnings); %2 classes this game does not have were left out. Save at Review puts them to use.

Paste config lines, a layout (Export, Layout only) or rules here with Ctrl+V. A layout, and the values of a class this game does not have, go to the class selected in the editor. They go into the draft; Undo takes them back.
Applied the layout to %1 (%2 warnings). Save at Review puts it to use.

Someone else saved the setup while you were working on it. Put your changes on top of theirs, or overwrite what they saved?
Keep these cells and this picture for this class. Save at Review puts them to use.
Keep these cells for this class and every class built on it, as one rule. A class with a rule of its own further down keeps it. Save at Review puts them to use.
Blocks puts compartments side by side: Apply here loses where they were painted.
Click a compartment's name to pick it, and a cell to make it a hole. The inventory puts compartments side by side.
Take every colour away and start again.
Paint every empty place in the brush colour.

Pick a uniform, vest, backpack, crate or kit on the left and draw its cells on the right. Apply keeps the change; Save at Review puts it to use. The search takes wildcards (B_Bergen*, *Carryall*); Tree shows everything built on a class, to change them all at once.
Its own cells are all its room - Enhanced First Aid Kits' capacity no longer counts. Back to the preset returns it to the capacity.

Enhanced First Aid Kits decides by its capacity now, and the kit window grows as needed. These cells are only a start: once Apply gives the kit cells of its own, they are all its room and the capacity no longer counts - in the inventory and in the ACE Arsenal. Back to the preset returns it to the capacity.
An old table setting decides this class and wins over every rule. Remove the class there for these cells to count.
Its own cells. Everything else is the same as %1.
Same as %1: these are its cells, and they change only there. Unlink to draw its own.
%1 holds nothing - there are no cells to draw.
Pick a colour, then click or drag over cells. Touching cells of one colour are one compartment; empty places are left out.
These cells come from its load or a pattern. A change here replaces that with exactly these cells.
Pick a container on the left to see and draw its cells.
Remove its own cells, the link to another class and its picture settings. The preset decides again.
Remove the cells of this class and of its tree, and the link to another class. The preset decides again; a class with a rule of its own keeps it.

Its cells must touch side by side or one above the other: an item is one piece.
Pick an item on the left to see and set its size.
Choose another picture for this item from the pictures of the game's items, or type the path of any texture.
